course.title: Java Backend with Spring Boot
course.subtitle: From domain model to deployed service
course.summary: Design the domain first, then build a Spring Boot service around it, with persistence, auth, tests and failure handling decided before the first endpoint.
overview: Plenty of Spring Boot material teaches you to annotate a class and get a JSON response. Far less of it explains why the resulting application becomes hard to change after six months.

This course builds a service in the order a working engineer should build one. Domain model, then persistence, then the API, then auth, then the failure cases. The framework shows up where it helps rather than driving the design.
whatYouWillLearn: Model a domain before writing a single endpoint
Use dependency injection deliberately instead of by reflex
Map entities with JPA without letting the ORM design your schema
Build REST APIs with versioning and error semantics decided up front
Add JWT authentication and role-based access without touching every controller
Write unit and integration tests that catch real regressions
Handle timeouts, retries and idempotency on write paths
